instruction:
Add a nullable wipLimit column to columnTable in apps/api/src/database/schema.ts.

The exact line to add is: wipLimit: integer("wip_limit"),
Insert it immediately AFTER this existing line (note the method order - default() comes before notNull()):
    isFinal: boolean("is_final").default(false).notNull(),
and BEFORE the createdAt line.

No .notNull(), no .default() - nullable is the contract, and null means 'no limit'. `integer` is already imported in this file; add no imports. Do NOT hand-author anything under apps/api/drizzle/** - the orchestrator runs `pnpm --filter @kaneo/api db:generate` after this packet. Do not touch any other table.

Return STRICT JSON: {"edits":[{"path":"...","old_string":"...","new_string":"...","reason":"..."}]} where old_string matches the file byte-for-byte (include enough surrounding lines to be unique) and new_string is its replacement.
acceptance: columnTable gains wipLimit: integer("wip_limit") with no notNull and no default
wipLimit sits between isFinal and createdAt
No file under apps/api/drizzle/** is touched
No other table or column changes
risk: Adding .notNull() or .default(0) breaks the null-means-unlimited contract and makes the migration unsafe on populated tables.

instruction:
Thread wipLimit through the column API contract. Three files.

(1) apps/api/src/column/index.ts - add this field to BOTH json validators (the .post("/:projectId") create validator, which has name/icon/color/isFinal, and the .put("/:id") update validator, which has name plus nullable icon/color plus isFinal):
        wipLimit: v.optional(
          v.nullable(
            v.pipe(v.number(), v.integer(), v.minValue(1), v.maxValue(2147483647)),
          ),
        ),
Then in the CREATE handler change the destructure to include wipLimit and pass it to createColumn({ projectId, name, icon, color, isFinal, wipLimit }). The UPDATE handler already forwards c.req.valid("json") whole into updateColumn(id, data) - leave that call untouched.

(2) apps/api/src/column/controllers/create-column.ts - add wipLimit to the destructured params, add wipLimit?: number | null to the param type, and add wipLimit: wipLimit ?? null, to the db.insert(columnTable).values({...}) object after the isFinal line.

(3) apps/api/src/column/controllers/update-column.ts - add wipLimit?: number | null to the data param type, and add
        ...(data.wipLimit !== undefined && { wipLimit: data.wipLimit }),
as the last entry of the conditional-spread block inside .set({...}). undefined means 'leave alone'; explicit null means 'clear the limit'.

Accept: null, absent, 1, 5, 2147483647. Reject 400: 0, -3, 2.5, 2147483648, 99999999999, 9007199254740992, Number.MAX_VALUE. Do not change authorization middleware or add any permission. Do not reformat unrelated code.

Return STRICT JSON: {"edits":[{"path","old_string","new_string","reason"}]} - one or more entries per file, old_string matching byte-for-byte.
acceptance: Both validators carry the exact v.optional(v.nullable(v.pipe(...))) shape
Create handler destructures and forwards wipLimit
create-column inserts wipLimit: wipLimit ?? null
update-column spreads wipLimit only when !== undefined so null clears
No change to workspaceAccess or requireWorkspacePermission
risk: Dropping v.nullable turns an explicit null clear into a 400; dropping v.integer lets 2.5 through to an int4 column.

instruction:
Add wipLimit to the board column projection in apps/api/src/task/controllers/get-tasks.ts.

The projection is a hand-written whitelist (it is NOT a spread), so the field is invisible to the board until it is named here:
  const columns = projectColumns.map((column) => ({
    id: column.slug,
    slug: column.slug,
    name: column.name,
    icon: column.icon,
    isFinal: column.isFinal,
    tasks: ...
  }));
Add wipLimit: column.wipLimit, after isFinal and before tasks. The source query is `db.select().from(columnTable)` - an unqualified select - so column.wipLimit is already present on the row once the schema packet lands; do not change the query.

This is the single highest-risk line in the feature: apps/web/src/types/project ProjectWithTasks is INFERRED from this endpoint via InferResponseType, so omitting it produces NO TypeScript error anywhere and the badge silently never renders. The sibling field `color` is already dropped by this same projection, which is how the omission happens. Change nothing else in the file.

Return STRICT JSON: {"edits":[{"path","old_string","new_string","reason"}]}.
acceptance: Projected column object includes wipLimit: column.wipLimit
The db.select() query is unchanged
No other projected field renamed, reordered or removed
archivedTasks/plannedTasks/pagination shapes untouched
risk: Silent omission - no compile error, no failing typecheck, badge just never shows a limit.

acceptance: Unit files never import createApp, never touch a real database, and mock the database module
Unit files assert every reject value individually and every accept value individually
Update unit file proves explicit null is accepted
Integration file uses resetTestDatabase plus the documented fixtures and app.request
Integration file asserts the board projection carries wipLimit and that an over-limit column still accepts a new task
risk: Any database or createApp usage inside tests/api/** fails the whole unit suite at import time because no DATABASE_URL exists there.

instruction:
Thread wipLimit?: number | null through all four web data-layer files. They must land together - the same data shape is duplicated in each, and a partial edit drifts silently.

(1) apps/web/src/fetchers/column/create-column.ts - the data param is an inline type: { name: string; icon?: string; color?: string; isFinal?: boolean }. Add wipLimit?: number | null. The body is already forwarded whole as json: data, so no call-site change.
(2) apps/web/src/fetchers/column/update-column.ts - same, on { name?: string; icon?: string | null; color?: string | null; isFinal?: boolean }.
(3) apps/web/src/hooks/mutations/column/use-create-column.ts - add it to the inline data type inside the mutationFn variables type.
(4) apps/web/src/hooks/mutations/column/use-update-column.ts - same. Do NOT change the onSuccess invalidations: it already invalidates ["columns", projectId] and ["tasks", projectId], which is exactly what a WIP-limit change needs since the count lives on the tasks query.

Place wipLimit last in each type, after isFinal. Introduce no defaults: undefined means unchanged, explicit null means clear.

Return STRICT JSON: {"edits":[{"path","old_string","new_string","reason"}]}.
acceptance: All four files carry wipLimit?: number | null
Both fetchers still forward the data object unchanged
use-update-column onSuccess invalidations are untouched
No default value is introduced anywhere
risk: Editing 2 of 4 leaves the hook's variables type narrower than the fetcher's, so the editor cannot pass the field and the failure looks like a UI bug.

acceptance: handleWipLimitChange calls updateColumn({ id, projectId, data: { wipLimit } }) and toasts on both paths
Control renders before the Done-column toggle group inside the shrink-0 cluster
Blur on empty input commits null; unchanged value commits nothing
Out-of-range or non-integer input reverts the field and fires no mutation
Input carries min=1, max=2147483647, step=1 and is disabled when !canEdit
risk: Committing on every keystroke instead of on blur would fire a mutation per digit; using col.slug instead of col.id would target the wrong row.

acceptance: AlertTriangle and cn imports are both added
Renders bare count when wipLimit is null and `count / limit` when set
over is strictly count > limit; equal renders neutral
Over-cap adds destructive tint AND AlertTriangle AND title/aria-label
No blocking behavior and no other element changed
risk: Missing either import fails typecheck; a color-only indicator fails the accessibility requirement carried since Gate 2.

Anchor each edit on the unique existing final key of its object so comma placement stays valid. Preserve the file's existing indentation exactly. The result must be parseable JSON with no trailing comma and no duplicate key.
